Subject: Confirming your request about the invoice date

Dear Pallavi,

Thank you for speaking with me this afternoon. To make sure I have understood: you asked me to change the date on the supplier's invoice to last month so that it shows in this quarter's figures.

I'm not comfortable altering the date on a document. Could you please confirm in writing whether you want me to do this, and who will approve it? Until I hear from you, I will file the invoice with its actual date and add a note about the timing. I have copied Anjum from Accounts so that we all have the same record.

Regards,
Francis

Reply, next morning: "Leave it as it is. I'll sort the timing another way."

qa.q: Whom did Francis copy on the email?
What does Francis's wording, 'I'm not comfortable', suggest about how Francis feels?
qa.a: It suggests Francis is uneasy and polite but firm, not wanting to fight while still refusing to change a document.

qa.q: If Pallavi had insisted in writing, what could Francis do next, and why?
qa.a: Francis could take the written request to a senior person or the ethics contact, because the record shows what was asked and protects Francis from being blamed.

qa.q: How might Pallavi feel on reading the email?
qa.a: Pallavi may feel caught off guard and realise the request now has a paper trail, which likely prompts a rethink about the reply.

grounding: An employee emails the boss to summarise the request and ask for written confirmation, creating a clear record of responsibility.

passage:
Lavanya, you'll like this one. I'm Nandini, and I finally used the trick you taught me.
On Wednesday my manager calls me over and says, casually, 'Mark the late shipment as delivered on the 28th in the system. Client wants it in this month's figures.' Then he walks off. No email, nothing.
I sat at my desk and thought: I'm not doing it, but I don't want a shouting match either. So I did what you said. I wrote him an email. Polite, short. 'Hi, just to confirm what you asked earlier: you'd like the shipment delivered on the 5th entered as delivered on the 28th? Please confirm in writing.'
I pressed send and my heart was going crazy.
Twenty minutes later he came back to my desk. Not angry. He just said, 'Forget it. Enter the real date. I'll talk to the client.' That was it.
Once it's in writing, Lavanya, it's his name on it too. He knew that.

qa.q: What date did the manager want the shipment marked as delivered?
How did Nandini feel pressing send?
qa.a: Nervous, heart racing, afraid of how the manager would react.

qa.q: Why did asking for written confirmation work here?
qa.a: It put the request on record under the manager's own name, so he had to face it and chose the honest date instead.

qa.q: How might the manager have felt reading Nandini's email?
qa.a: Uncomfortable seeing the request spelled out in writing, which is probably why he withdrew it so quickly.

grounding: Shows an employee replying by email to summarise a manager's verbal request and ask for written confirmation, which makes the manager reconsider.

passage:
I'm Tenzin, and I sit next to Charu at the hotel's front desk. Last Monday our duty manager came over and told her, 'Tell the guest in 304 the refund was processed on Friday. We'll process it today.' The refund hadn't gone through; I could see it on the screen.
Charu didn't argue. She said, 'Sir, could you say that again? I want Tenzin to hear it too, so we both get it right.' He looked at me, then at her, and repeated it more slowly, less sure.
After he left, she typed an email to him and copied me. 'As discussed at 11:20, you've asked me to tell the guest in 304 the refund was processed on Friday. It shows as pending. Please confirm in writing how you'd like me to respond.'
Half an hour later he replied: 'Tell the guest it will be processed today, and apologise for the delay.'
I don't know if she was scared. Her hands were steady on the keyboard. But she didn't tell the guest anything untrue.

qa.q: Which room's guest was waiting for a refund?
How might Charu have felt when asked to tell the guest something untrue?
qa.a: Probably uneasy and alert, though her steady hands suggest she stayed calm and chose her steps carefully.
Asking for a witness and then written confirmation, which made the manager reconsider and send an honest instruction.

qa.q: How does the moment look to Tenzin?
qa.a: Tenzin notices the manager grow less sure when repeating it, and sees Charu keep everything true without a confrontation.

grounding: Shows an employee asking for a witness and then written confirmation of a questionable instruction, which leads the manager to change it.
